title: 第292章 回家了第291章 永恒空间
content_zh:
王建新从海上往京城飞的时候，天已经快黑了。
他飞得不快，一边飞一边想事情。这次突破金丹期，收获大得他自己都觉得不真实。一千二百年的寿命，永恒空间，时间法则，还有那一大堆功法。这些东西随便拿出一样来，都够让人瞠目结舌的了，现在全堆在他一个人身上。
他低头看了看脚下的大地。从高空中往下看，城市的灯光星星点点，像撒了一地的碎金子。远处的山影影绰绰，近处的田野一块一块的，被暮色笼罩着。这片土地他太熟悉了，每一寸都跑过、看过、守护过。
他放慢了速度，在京城上空转了一圈。天安门广场上的灯已经亮了，长安街上的车流像一条火龙，从西边蜿蜒到东边。他看着这些，心里头说不出的踏实。不管他在外面经历了什么，回到这儿，心就安了。
他没有从正门进去，而是直接落在了自家四合院的后院里。
院子里静悄悄的。天已经黑透了，廊下的灯亮着，昏黄的光洒在地上。王建新站在院子中间，深吸了一口气。家里头那股熟悉的味道——饭香、花香、还有囡囡身上那股奶香味，混在一起，让他鼻子有点发酸。
他往前院走，刚转过月亮门，就听见了囡囡的笑声。
小丫头正在院子里追蝴蝶。那是一只白色的粉蝶，不知道从哪儿飞来的，在花丛间忽上忽下地飞着。囡囡穿着一件红色的小裙子，扎着两个小揪揪，迈着两条小短腿，跑得气喘吁吁的，嘴里喊着“蝴蝶别跑、蝴蝶别跑”。
王建新站在那儿，看着女儿的背影，眼泪差点掉下来。
他不在的这段时间，小丫头好像又长高了一点。头发也长长了，跑起来的时候两个小揪揪一颠一颠的，可爱得不行。
囡囡追着蝴蝶跑了两圈，没追上，气鼓鼓地停下来，一转身，看见了王建新。
小丫头愣了一下。
她揉了揉眼睛，又看了一眼。然后——
“爸爸！”
囡囡像一颗小炮弹一样冲了过来，扑进王建新怀里，搂着他的脖子，把脸埋在他肩膀上，哇的一声就哭了。
“爸爸你去哪了，囡囡想你了，囡囡天天想你了……”
王建新把孩子抱起来，紧紧地搂在怀里，一只手拍着她的后背，声音有点哑：“爸爸也想囡囡了，爸爸回来了，不走了。”
囡囡哭得稀里哗啦的，眼泪鼻涕糊了王建新一肩膀。小丫头一边哭一边嘟囔：“你说去几天就回来的，你骗人，你去了好久好久……”
王建新抱着她，在院子里来回走，嘴里哄着：“是爸爸不好，爸爸以后不骗囡囡了。”
囡囡哭了好一会儿才停下来，抽抽搭搭的，小手紧紧抓着王建新的衣领，生怕他再跑了。

这时候小梅从屋里出来了。
她应该是听见了囡囡的哭声，端着个碗，围着围裙，头发随便扎在脑后。看见王建新的那一刻，她整个人僵住了，手里的碗差点掉在地上。
王建新看着她，笑了笑：“我回来了。”
小梅的眼泪一下子就涌了出来。她把碗放在廊下的台阶上，快步走过来，走到王建新面前，停住了。她伸手摸了摸他的脸，好像要确认这是不是真的。然后她张了张嘴，想说什么，又没说，眼泪止不住地往下掉。
王建新一手抱着囡囡，一手把小梅搂进怀里。
小梅把脸埋在他胸口，哭得浑身发抖。她没出声，就那么默默地哭着，泪水把王建新的衣服打湿了一大片。
囡囡被夹在中间，看看爸爸，看看妈妈，也跟着又哭了起来。一家三口就那么站在院子里，抱成一团，哭了好一会儿。
最后是小梅先止住了。她抬起头，用袖子擦了擦眼泪，声音还有点哑：“吃饭了没？”
“没呢。”王建新说。
“我去给你热。”小梅转身进了厨房，走了两步又回头看了他一眼，好像怕他消失似的。
王建新抱着囡囡跟了进去。
厨房里热气腾腾的，灶台上坐着锅，咕嘟咕嘟地冒着泡。小梅揭开锅盖，是一锅排骨汤，炖得浓白，香味扑鼻。她又从柜子里拿出几个馒头，放在蒸笼上热着。
“你不在的这些天，妈天天念叨你。”小梅一边忙活一边说，声音已经平静下来了，“大哥二哥也问了好几回，说你那个任务怎么还没完。我跟他们说，我也不知道。”
王建新坐在厨房的小板凳上，囡囡坐在他腿上，已经不哭了，但小手还是抓着他的衣服不撒开。他听着小梅说话，看着她在灶台前忙活的背影，心里头暖洋洋的。
content_en:
When Wang Jianxin flew from the sea to the capital, it was almost dark.
He didn't fly very fast, thinking about things while flying. Breaking through the golden elixir stage this time, the harvest was so great that he felt it was unreal. One thousand two hundred years of life, eternal space, the law of time, and a lot of skills. Any of these things would be enough to stun people, but now they were all piled on him alone.
He looked down at the ground beneath his feet. Looking down from the sky, the city lights are dotted like scattered gold. The mountains in the distance are shadowy, and the fields nearby are covered in twilight. He was very familiar with this land. He had run through, seen and guarded every inch of it.
He slowed down and circled around the capital. The lights on Tiananmen Square have been turned on, and the traffic on Chang'an Street is like a fire dragon, winding from west to east. Looking at these, he felt indescribably at ease. No matter what he went through outside, he felt at ease when he came back here.
He did not go in through the main entrance, but landed directly in the backyard of his courtyard house.
The yard was quiet. It was already dark, the lights in the corridor were on, and a dim light fell on the ground. Wang Jianxin stood in the middle of the yard and took a deep breath. The familiar smells at home—the smell of rice, flowers, and the smell of milk from his daughter—mixed together to make his nose feel a little sore.
He walked to the front yard, and as soon as he turned around the moon gate, he heard his daughter's laughter.
The little girl is chasing butterflies in the yard. It was a white butterfly that flew from nowhere, flying up and down among the flowers. Nannan was wearing a little red skirt, tied with two little knots, and running on two short legs, panting, shouting "Butterfly, don't run, butterfly, don't run."
Wang Jianxin stood there, looking at his daughter's back, almost crying.
During his absence, the little girl seemed to have grown a little taller. The hair has also grown longer, and the two little ones bounce around when they run, which is so cute.
Nannan ran after the butterfly twice, but failed to catch up. She stopped angrily, turned around, and saw Wang Jianxin.
The little girl was stunned for a moment.
She rubbed her eyes and looked again. Then——
"Dad!"
Nannan rushed over like a small cannonball, threw herself into Wang Jianxin's arms, hugged his neck, buried her face in his shoulder, and cried with a cry.
"Dad, where have you been? I miss you. I miss you every day..."
Wang Jianxin picked up the child and held her tightly in his arms. He patted her back with one hand and said in a hoarse voice, "Dad misses me too. Daddy is back and won't leave."
Nannan cried so hard that Wang Jianxin's shoulders were covered with tears and runny nose. The little girl cried and muttered: "You said you would be back in a few days. You lied. You were gone for a long time..."
Wang Jianxin held her in his arms and walked back and forth in the yard, coaxing: "It's dad's fault. Dad won't lie to my daughter anymore."
Nannan cried for a while before she stopped, twitching and holding on to Wang Jianxin's collar with her little hands, for fear that he would run away again.
At this time Xiaomei came out of the house.
She must have heard her daughter's cry. She was holding a bowl, wearing an apron, and her hair tied back casually. The moment she saw Wang Jianxin, she froze and almost dropped the bowl in her hand.
Wang Jianxin looked at her and smiled: "I'm back."
Xiaomei's tears burst out all of a sudden. She put the bowl on the steps of the corridor, walked over quickly, stopped in front of Wang Jianxin. She reached out and touched his face, as if to confirm if this was true. Then she opened her mouth, wanting to say something, but she didn't say anything, and her tears couldn't stop falling.
Wang Jianxin held his daughter in one hand and Xiaomei in his arms with the other.
Xiaomei buried her face in his chest, crying so hard that her whole body was shaking. She didn't make a sound, just cried silently,Tears wet a large area of ​​Wang Jianxin's clothes.
Nanny was caught in the middle. She looked at her father and mother, and started crying again. The family of three just stood in the yard, hugging each other and crying for a long time.
In the end, it was Xiaomei who stopped first. She raised her head and wiped her tears with her sleeve, her voice still a little hoarse: "Have you eaten yet?"
"No." Wang Jianxin said.
"I'll heat it up for you." Xiaomei turned around and entered the kitchen. After taking two steps, she looked back at him, as if she was afraid that he would disappear.
Wang Jianxin followed Nannan in his arms.
The kitchen was steaming, and there was a pot sitting on the stove, bubbling. Xiaomei opened the lid and found a pot of pork ribs soup, stewed thickly and white, with a fragrant aroma. She took out a few steamed buns from the cabinet and placed them on the steamer to heat them.
"These days when you are away, mom talks about you every day." Xiaomei said while busy, her voice has calmed down, "The eldest brother and the second brother also asked several times why you haven't finished the task. I told them, I don't know."
Wang Jianxin was sitting on the small bench in the kitchen, and his daughter was sitting on his lap. She had stopped crying, but her little hands were still holding on to his clothes. He listened to Xiaomei's words and looked at her back working in front of the stove, feeling warm in his heart.
